name: agda
why: A dependently typed language where types are proofs, a genuinely strange way to program and prove things.

brief.what_it_is: Agda is a dependently typed functional programming language and interactive proof assistant. It lets you write programs whose types can depend on values, such as a type of vectors indexed by length, and then check proofs about those programs. The homepage describes an interactive Emacs interface that helps the programmer write code, and the brew description calls it a dependently typed functional programming language. Input is Agda source code; the checker verifies types and proofs, and the compiler produces executables. The package installs four executables: agda, agda-mode, agda2hs, and als.
brief.why_it_exists: The wiki frames Agda as a foundational tool for constructive mathematics based on Per Martin-Löf's intuitionistic type theory, and as a system for writing and checking proofs interactively. It is positioned alongside other dependent-type proof assistants such as Rocq, Epigram, Matita and NuPRL.
brief.how_it_works: Agda type-checks programs and proofs written in dependently typed functional style, supporting inductive families, parametrised modules, mixfix operators and Unicode. The main interactive workflow runs through an Emacs interface (agda-mode) that assists the programmer while writing the program. The GitHub README points to a 'Quick guide to editing, type checking and compiling Agda code' as the entry point for this workflow.
brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the brew caveats say that to use installed Agda libraries you must run: mkdir -p $HOME/.config/agda, then copy $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/opt/agda/share/agda/example-libraries to $HOME/.config/agda/libraries and example-defaults to $HOME/.config/agda/defaults. Redo this after upgrading from an earlier version. The Agda Pad lets you try Agda in the browser without installing. The Agda Standard Library is a separate download with its own wiki page.
brief.standout: Types are proofs: a single language is both the programming language and the proof checker, so a program can carry a machine-checked specification in its type. Agda also has an interactive editor-driven workflow in Emacs, with Unicode syntax and mixfix operators, which makes it feel quite unlike mainstream languages. The agda2hs executable, bundled here, translates Agda code to Haskell.
brief.status: maintained. The wiki lists Agda Standard Library 2.4 released 2026-06-17 and Version 2.8.0 released 2025-07-05. The wiki page was last modified August 07, 2026. Agda Implementors' Meetings are scheduled for April 2026 and October 2026. The GitHub README shows active CI badges and links to a user manual and CHANGELOG.
brief.caveats: The brew caveats say the library setup needs manual copying into ~/.config/agda and must be redone after upgrades. The GitHub README is only about Agda itself and not the standard library, which is documented separately on the wiki. The wiki homepage is a PmWiki page and was readable only as plain text, so I did not verify the install page or the tutorials directly. The scout note says the language is strange to program in, which matches the wiki's emphasis on proofs; this is a learning curve, not a stated caveat from the authors.
quotes: Agda is a dependently typed functional programming language. It has inductive families, i.e., data types which depend on values, such as the type of vectors of a given length.
Agda is a proof assistant. It is an interactive system for writing and checking proofs.
Agda is open-source and enjoys contributions from many authors.
